notes: The seven duplicate records all identify the legendary ruler Yu (禹), also styled Great Yu (大禹). Shiji 36 explicitly calls him Xiahou Yu, while the later histories cite the same sage-king as an ancient precedent.
Both records identify Later Tang official Suo Zitong (索自通); the shared Zitong is his given name, not a reference to Han Qinhu's or Li Yu's courtesy name.

Shiji 109 explicitly identifies Li Yu as Li Gan's son and a favored member of the crown prince's household. New Book of Tang 70 gives the same father-son link in the Longxi Li genealogy and adds Li Yu's courtesy name Zitong. Its broad generated date interval is a lineage estimate; Shiji's BC 118-100 attestation is the controlling chronology.

These records respectively identify Yu the Great (禹/大禹), Li Yu (李禹) styled Zitong and son of Li Gan, Sui general Han Qinhu (韓擒虎) styled Zitong, and Later Tang official Suo Zitong (索自通). Zitong is a courtesy name for two of them and part of Suo's personal name, while Yu is a different personal name in the Li genealogy.
This decision names the exact members of the unresolved English Zitong block: Later Tang Suo Zitong, Sui general Han Qinhu styled Zitong, and Western Han Li Yu styled Zitong.
